Question B-006-010-005.

Why the correct answer is right: A quarter-wave vertical on a car roof is vertically oriented over a ground plane, so its azimuth pattern is essentially omnidirectional: it radiates equally well in all horizontal directions around the vehicle.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Most of it goes vertically straight-up": A vertical over a ground plane is not intended to send most energy straight up; the useful radiation is outward around the horizon.
- sourceIndex 2: "Most of it goes equally in two opposite directions": That describes a two-lobed broadside pattern such as a simple dipole, not the circular azimuth pattern of a vertical whip.
- sourceIndex 3: "Most of it goes in one direction": A single quarter-wave vertical on a car roof is not a beam. Without directors or a phased array it has no preferred compass direction.
